scenicChapters.title: Grand Tour of Switzerland
scenicChapters.narrative: Water arrives beside the road and stays for 25 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go — slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did.

scenicChapters.title: Grand Tour of Switzerland
scenicChapters.narrative: For 37 km this is Grand Tour of Switzerland, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it. Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

road-grand-tour-of-switzerland-arc.story: 1032 km from Zürich to Bussigny, about 15 h 59 of riding. On the way it passes Schaffhausen, Bodensee, St. Gallen and Appenzell. The highest point is about 2,450 m. Fluela Pass is subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. It crosses Switzerland, Liechtenstein and Italy - carry ID and check vignette or toll rules. It suits an unhurried touring pace.

portillo-and-los-libertadores.title: Portillo and Los Libertadores
portillo-and-los-libertadores.slogan: The old road to Argentina: thirty numbered hairpins stacked up the Caracoles to three thousand metres.

waypoints.name: Los Andes
waypoints.advice: Los Andes is where the day begins. Next is Río Blanco, climbing 600 m.

waypoints.name: Río Blanco
waypoints.advice: Río Blanco comes up 32 km in. The road climbs 600 m on the way up to it, steadily. Reckon on about 4 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Next is Portillo, climbing 1460 m.

waypoints.name: Portillo
waypoints.advice: 64 km in you reach Portillo. The road climbs 1460 m on the way up to it, hard. Reckon on about 13 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Next is Caracoles, climbing 320 m.

waypoints.name: Caracoles
waypoints.advice: The high point of this section, 3200 m up. The road climbs 320 m on the way up to it, steadily. Reckon on about 15 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Nothing on this route is higher. At this height the road is a summer one: snow gates can stay shut into June and shut again in October.

portillo-and-los-libertadores.provenance: MANUAL SEED: every stop was entered by hand from a known position on the road. The distance is the seed figure, not a routed measurement - the pipeline replaces it. Altitudes are present only where they were known; the rest are null rather than zero.

scenicChapters.title: Los Andes → Río Blanco
scenicChapters.narrative: The ground tilts up and stays tilted for 56 km. 600 m of it, taken steadily rather than in one wall. A steady rhythm suits this better than bursts. The height arrives whether you hurry or not.

scenicChapters.title: Paso de los Libertadores
scenicChapters.narrative: First and second gear more often than not. Look through each corner to the next one and let the engine do the holding. The valley floor is behind you and the road starts working for its height at about 6.7%. Corners stack above one another where the ground allows nothing straighter.

scenicChapters.title: Paso de los Libertadores
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 3200 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance — cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

portillo-and-los-libertadores.story: 96 km from Los Andes to the finish, about 1 h 51 of riding. On the way it passes Río Blanco and Portillo. The climb of the day is Caracoles. It tops out at 3,200 m. Cristo Redentor Pass is subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. It crosses from Chile into Argentina - carry ID and check vignette or toll rules. It was put together for the scenery rather than the shortest line.
